name: Low-Carb Turkey Cauliflower Mushroom Casserole

ingredients.buy: about 3 lb, roasted and diced (about 7 cups cooked)

prose.intro_html: Casserole usually starts with a can of cream-of-something soup and ends with a sleeve of crackers on top, and both of those are just cheap carbs in a dinner costume. This one earns the name the honest way. Roasted turkey breast, browned mushrooms, softened onion, and riced cauliflower get folded into a real sauce built from sour cream, mayo, Dijon, and two kinds of cheese, then the whole thing bakes under a blanket of mozzarella until it browns. No soup can, no breadcrumbs, no flour. Built at 14 servings it runs about {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein a serving, with under 15 grams of carbs. That is comfort food that works for your body and your wallet at the same time.
shop_smart: About three pounds of turkey breast is the anchor. The source leans on leftover holiday turkey, but you do not have to wait for a holiday. Buy a raw turkey breast, roast it yourself, and dice it into bite-sized pieces. This is where most of the protein and most of the money live, so buy the plain breast and skip the pre-seasoned deli stuff you would pay extra for.

Two heads of cauliflower do the job the rice used to. You want fresh heads chopped and pulsed into a rice texture, which browns up in the pan and carries the bulk of the dish without carrying the carbs. Frozen riced cauliflower works too if that is what your store keeps stocked, and it saves you the food processor.

Mushrooms and onion build the base. Just under two pounds of sliced crimini mushrooms and a couple of onions get browned down first and layered in the bottom of the dish. Cooking the water out of the mushrooms before they go in is what keeps the finished casserole from turning soupy.

Sour cream, mayo, and Dijon make the sauce, not a soup can. Full-fat sour cream and mayo bring the richness, the Dijon brings the tang, and grated mozzarella and a little parmesan melt in to bind it. Reach for full-fat here on purpose; the light versions water the sauce down and this dish is built to hold its calories.

Thyme and poultry seasoning are the whole spice rack you need. A few teaspoons of each, split between the cauliflower and the sauce, is what makes a pile of turkey and vegetables taste like Thanksgiving dinner. These are jars you buy once and cook with all season long.
make_it: Weigh your empty baking dish and write the number down. You will need it at the end to split this into 14 even servings by weight, which is the only honest way to portion one big bake.

Rub the turkey breast with a little salt and pepper and roast it at 375 degrees F until the center reads 165, about 45 minutes for a 3 pound breast. Let it rest, then dice it into bite-sized pieces, about 7 cups.

Make the sauce while the turkey rests. In a big bowl, stir together the sour cream, mayo, and Dijon with the smaller share of the thyme and poultry seasoning, half of the grated mozzarella, and all of the parmesan until it is smooth.

Heat a third of the olive oil in your largest skillet over medium-high heat and cook the sliced mushrooms until the liquid cooks off and they brown, about 6 to 8 minutes. Spread them across the bottom of the baking dish.
Add another third of the oil and cook the chopped onion until it softens and starts to color, about 5 minutes. Scatter it over the mushrooms.

Add the last of the oil and cook the riced cauliflower over medium-high heat, stirring often, until it softens and barely browns, about 4 minutes. Stir in the larger share of the thyme and poultry seasoning and a good pinch of salt and pepper, cook one more minute, then layer it into the dish.

Scatter the diced turkey over the vegetables and fold everything together, then spread the sauce over the top and fold again until every piece is coated. Level it off and blanket it with the rest of the mozzarella.
Bake uncovered at 375 degrees F until it is bubbling and the top is nicely browned, about 40 minutes. Let it rest a few minutes so it firms up, then weigh the dish and portion as below.
prose.portion_html: Set the baked dish on your scale and subtract the empty weight you wrote down in Step 1 to get the total. Divide that number by 14 and scoop that exact weight into each container. Every serving lands near {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.
prose.cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a serving (at everyday cost) for a baked, bubbling casserole that eats like the soup-can version and skips the carbs. The turkey and the cheese carry the protein; the cauliflower and mushrooms do the job the rice and the noodles used to, for a lot less.

head.description: Low-carb turkey cauliflower mushroom casserole for meal prep: roasted turkey breast, riced cauliflower, and browned mushrooms baked in a real sour cream and mozzarella sauce with no soup can and no flour, built for 14 servings. About {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein per serving, with under 15 grams of carbs.
head.keywords: turkey cauliflower casserole, low carb turkey casserole, keto casserole, cauliflower rice casserole, mushroom casserole, high protein meal prep
steps: Weigh the empty baking dish and note the number for portioning later.
Roast the turkey breast at 375 degrees F to 165 in the center, rest, and dice into about 7 cups.
Stir together the sour cream, mayo, Dijon, some of the thyme and poultry seasoning, half the mozzarella, and all the parmesan to make the sauce.
Brown the sliced mushrooms in olive oil and spread them in the bottom of the dish.
Soften the chopped onion in olive oil and scatter it over the mushrooms.
Cook the riced cauliflower in olive oil with the rest of the thyme and poultry seasoning, salt, and pepper, then layer it in.
Fold in the diced turkey and the sauce, top with the rest of the mozzarella, and bake at 375 degrees F for about 40 minutes until bubbling, then rest, weigh, and divide across 14 containers.
